originalTitle: RBI to close FCNR(B) swaps a month earlier due to gush
simplifiedContent: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to end a special deposit program called FCNR(B) a month earlier than planned, on August 31. This is because the program has been very successful and has brought in more foreign money than expected. The RBI had allowed people to swap their money into these deposits, and many people took advantage of this, which led to a lot of money flowing in. As a result, the RBI has decided to close this program early, but other similar programs will continue as planned. This change is important because it shows that the RBI's efforts to attract foreign money are working, which can have a positive impact on the economy.

originalTitle: Wall St Week Ahead: With US Fed silent on next move, investors look to earnings to keep stocks afloat
simplifiedContent: The US stock market is waiting to see what the Federal Reserve (the "US Fed") will do next, but for now, they're not saying anything. Because of this uncertainty, investors are looking at how well companies are doing financially to decide whether to buy or sell stocks. Luckily, many companies are reporting strong earnings, especially those that are investing in artificial intelligence, which is making investors more confident in the market. This good news is currently more important to investors than worries about the overall economy and inflation. As a result, the strong earnings are helping to keep the stock market stable for now.

originalTitle: US stock: S&P 500 ends lower as investors weigh data, Middle East tensions
simplifiedContent: The US stock market, measured by the S&P 500, went down recently. This happened because people are worried about how well consumers are spending money, based on weaker retail sales numbers. Some individual stocks, like Applied Materials, also did poorly, which affected other similar stocks. On the other hand, energy companies did well because oil prices are going up. Additionally, Reddit's stock price went up after it was announced that it would be included in a certain index.

originalTitle: RVNL vs IRFC vs IRCON vs IRCTC: Which railway stock to buy after Q1 results 2026?
simplifiedContent: Some companies related to the railway industry in India just released their first quarter results for 2026. Experts think that IRFC is a good representation of the government's spending on railways because it has government backing. RVNL and IRCON are companies that build things like roads and bridges, while IRCTC is a company that has a monopoly on certain services. This information can help investors decide which of these railway-related companies to invest in. It's worth considering because these companies' performances can indicate how the railway industry is doing overall.

originalTitle: Stocks to buy under  ₹200: Mehul Kothari of Anand Rathi recommends three shares to buy or sell
simplifiedContent: Mehul Kothari, an expert from a company called Anand Rathi, has given some advice on which stocks to buy or sell. He has recommended three specific stocks: IRB Infra, MMTC, and CESC. What's notable about these stocks is that they are all currently priced under ₹200. This means that investors can buy these stocks without having to spend a lot of money. The recommendation from Mehul Kothari may be helpful for investors who are looking for affordable stocks to invest in.

originalTitle: These 5 stocks are paying out more than their profits in dividends
simplifiedContent: Some companies are paying out more in dividends to their investors than they are making in profits. This means they are giving their investors more money than they are actually earning. This can be a sign that the companies have a lot of cash on hand, but it also raises concerns about whether they can keep paying out so much without hurting their ability to grow in the future. Investors should be cautious and evaluate whether these companies can sustain their high dividend payments. It's essential for investors to understand this to make informed decisions about their investments.
